text.p: Shares of Deutsche Telekom were oversubscribed 73 times in Austria, Creditanstalt, the only Austrian member among the consortium of lead managers, said on Monday.
Austrian investors signed for shares worth about seven billion schillings, but a paltry 1.37 percent of bids were filled, the bank said in a statement.
The issue as a whole, worth some 20 billion marks based on the issue price of 28.50 marks per share, was oversubscribed by about five times.
"The tranche for the 'rest of Europe' only accounts for six percent of the total issue to help satisfy the huge demand for Telekom shares by German private investors," the bank said.
This part of the offering covered all European countries except Germany and the U.K., it added.
Austrian investors who had signed up for what is Europe's largest-ever initial public offering would receive shares on a first-come, first-serve basis, Creditanstalt said.
About one third of the 713 million shares issued were taken up by foreign investors. More than half of the total was expected to be snapped up by institutional buyers.
Telekom unit DeTeMobil is part of an international consortium that operates Austria's first mobile phone network, max.mobil. -- Vienna newsroom +431 53112 274
